Title: Spatially resolved multiomics on the neuronal effects induced by spaceflight in mice
One sentence finding: Spaceflight induced region- and cell-associated molecular changes in mouse brain.
One sentence remaining question: Which brain signatures reproduce independently across other missions and cell-type datasets?
Notes: NASA publications archive lists OSD-352; original article DOI.

Title: Behavioral and multiomics analysis of 3D clinostat simulated microgravity effect in mice focusing on the central nervous system
One sentence finding: Simulated microgravity affected mouse CNS behaviour and molecular profiles in a multiomics study.
One sentence remaining question: Which reported responses also occur during actual spaceflight rather than clinostat simulation?
Notes: NASA archive lists OSD-32 and OSD-352; original study includes new simulated microgravity data.

Title: Effects of Space Flight on Inflammasome Activation in the Brain of Mice
One sentence finding: RR-1 mouse brains showed reduced caspase-1, ASC and IL-1β protein markers after spaceflight.
One sentence remaining question: Are these inflammasome changes reproducible and associated with specific cells or behavioural changes?
Notes: NASA archive lists OSD-738, OSD-751 and OSD-752.

Title: Automated behavioral segmentation and markerless pose tracking of mice during spaceflight
One sentence finding: Automated pose tracking and behavioural classification characterised RR-1 mouse flight videos.
One sentence remaining question: Which neural processes correspond to the classified behaviours, and are they reproducible in other missions?
Notes: OSDR video page and 2026 preprint are associated; peer review not assumed.

Title: Behavior of mice aboard the International Space Station
One sentence finding: ISS mice displayed organised race-tracking or circling, with age-related behavioural differences.
One sentence remaining question: Which neural mechanisms underlie circling, beyond the improved video phenotyping already available?
Notes: Paper is real; exact RR-1 video correspondence to OSD-952 not proven.

Title: MiRNAs shape mouse age-independent tissue adaptation to spaceflight via ECM and developmental pathways
One sentence finding: Spaceflight-associated miRNA changes across mouse tissues, including brain, implicated ECM and developmental regulation.
One sentence remaining question: Can brain miRNA associations be independently localised to specific CNS cell populations without assuming causality?
Notes: OSD-916 NASA record includes original 2026 paper; do not equate RNA correlations with target validation.

Title: Spaceflight-Induced Gene Expression Profiles in the Mouse Brain Are Attenuated by Treatment with the Antioxidant BuOE
One sentence finding: The antioxidant BuOE attenuated many spaceflight-associated regional brain transcriptional changes.
One sentence remaining question: Does the antioxidant-induced RNA response correspond to direct functional neuroprotection and suppression of ferroptotic cell damage?
Notes: Original antioxidant paper linked to four regional OSDR studies.

Title: Artificial gravity partially protects space-induced neurological deficits in Drosophila melanogaster
One sentence finding: Artificial gravity partly mitigated Drosophila flight-associated neuronal, glial and locomotor abnormalities.
One sentence remaining question: Which molecular modules explain this partial protection, and can they be validated beyond the original fly experiment?
Notes: NASA archive lists multi-modal Drosophila accessions.

Title: Characterization of gene expression profiles in the mouse brain after 35 days of spaceflight mission
One sentence finding: RR-9 brain profiling revealed changes in neuroimmune, stress, metabolic and synaptic gene-expression programmes.
One sentence remaining question: Which brain-cell compartments underlie the RR-9 response, and do independently observed cell-type signals predict neurovascular dysfunction?
Notes: NASA OSD-536 Publications section lists paper.

Title: Spaceflight induces oxidative damage to blood-brain barrier integrity in a mouse model
One sentence finding: RR-9 mice showed hippocampal apoptosis-related and blood–brain barrier marker changes following spaceflight.
One sentence remaining question: Are neurovascular and neuroimmune changes linked in the same animals, rather than merely the same mission?
Notes: NASA OSD-898 Publications section lists original paper.

Title: Postsynaptic density radiation signature following space irradiation
One sentence finding: Radiation exposure was associated with cognitive outcomes and hippocampal molecular signatures across particle conditions.
One sentence remaining question: Does the reported signature predict outcomes in an independent radiation cohort not analysed in the paper?
Notes: NASA OSD-611 Publications section lists paper.

Title: Three-dimensional spatial selectivity of hippocampal neurons during space flight
Type: Original historic; OSDR accession newly released
One sentence finding: Hippocampal neurons maintained spatial representations across differently oriented surfaces during spaceflight.
One sentence remaining question: Which circuit-level mechanisms enable three-dimensional spatial coding in microgravity?
Notes: OSD-968 NASA record lists paper and original electrophysiology file formats.

Title: Effects of 5-Ion Beam Irradiation and Hindlimb Unloading on Metabolic Pathways in Plasma and Brain of Behaviorally Tested WAG/Rij Rats
One sentence finding: A rat study jointly examined brain metabolites and behaviour after simulated space exposures.
One sentence remaining question: Do the reported metabolic–behaviour associations generalise to an independent cohort or exposure design?
Notes: Dataset titles link study to OSD-833, -834, -835; individual matching unknown.

Title: Deficits in Sustained Attention and Changes in Dopaminergic Protein Levels following Exposure to Proton Radiation Are Related to Basal Dopaminergic Function
Type: Original historic; OSDR accession newly released
One sentence finding: Proton irradiation affected sustained attention and regional dopaminergic proteins in a strain-dependent manner.
One sentence remaining question: Can baseline dopaminergic state predict vulnerability independently of genetic background?
Notes: NASA dataset/title records match paper and assay series.

Title: Spaceflight influences gene expression, photoreceptor integrity, and oxidative stress-related damage in the murine retina
One sentence finding: Spaceflight altered mouse retinal expression, photoreceptor integrity and oxidative-stress markers.
One sentence remaining question: Do similar vascular or stress pathways appear in brain tissue, without conflating retina with CNS?
Notes: OSD-255 study/paper association from earlier OSDR audit.

Title: Machine Learning Ensemble Reveals Distinct Molecular Pathways of Retinal Damage in Spaceflown Mice
One sentence finding: A 2026 preprint used machine learning to analyse retinal damage-related pathways in OSDR datasets.
One sentence remaining question: Can its retinal signatures be validated against independent experiments or a distinct assay modality?
Notes: NASA publication archive lists three OSDR accessions.

Title: Integrated cross-species translation and biophysical multi-scale modeling links molecular signatures and locomotory phenotypes in spaceflight-induced sarcopenia
One sentence finding: Cross-species modelling linked spaceflight muscle signatures to locomotor phenotypes.
One sentence remaining question: Which locomotor alterations are driven by central neural processes rather than peripheral muscle dysfunction?
Notes: NASA archive lists OSD-478; primarily musculoskeletal, not brain.

Title: Molecular effects of spaceflight in the mouse eye after space shuttle mission STS-135
One sentence finding: Spaceflight increased retinal oxidative damage staining and altered 139 retinal genes involving stress, inflammatory and neural pathways.
One sentence remaining question: Which of these retinal molecular responses recur in independent spaceflight experiments or translate into measurable visual dysfunction?
Notes: OSD-87 Publications tab lists DOI and same title; DOI confirmed externally.

Title: Neuroprotective Effects of Cerium Oxide Nanoparticles During Spaceflight
Type: Candidate — accession link not yet verified
One sentence finding: A 2026 study reported neuroprotective effects of cerium oxide nanoparticles in spaceflight-exposed neuron-like cells.
One sentence remaining question: Does transcriptomic and structural rescue by nanoceria persist in functional neural assays and independent in vivo models?
Evidence status: Peer-reviewed paper; experiment association strongly supported; OSD-level identifier still needs direct series match
Notes: OSD-1005 is labelled PROMETEO 2 and the 2026 Small Science paper reports PROMETEO 2 with GEO GSE295652; explicit NASA OSD-1005-to-GSE295652 metadata could not be retrieved.

Title: Characterization of mouse ocular response to a 35-day spaceflight mission: Evidence of blood-retinal barrier disruption and ocular adaptations
One sentence finding: RR-9 spaceflight mice showed retinal apoptosis and blood–retinal barrier-associated changes.
One sentence remaining question: Which vascular stress responses are shared with brain tissue and which are retina-specific?
Notes: NASA record associated with original RR-9 ocular barrier endpoints.

Title: Spaceflight modulates neurodegeneration-associated transcriptomic pathways across brain cell types
One sentence finding: Reanalysis of OSD-613 found spaceflight-associated neurodegeneration-related transcriptional programs, mitochondrial stress and early neuroimmune engagement across brain cell types.
One sentence remaining question: Do these cell-type transcriptional signatures predict measurable neurodegeneration or functional deficits?
Notes: Original 2026 article explicitly names OSD-613 and describes 4 groups; transcription does not prove disease.

Title: Sex-Specific Changes in Brain Organoids from Acute Simulated Galactic Cosmic Radiation are Rescued by Targeted ECM Pathway Stimulation
One sentence finding: Human brain organoids showed sex-associated radiation response patterns, and experimental FGFR-pathway stimulation mitigated selected changes.
One sentence remaining question: Do these protective effects generalise to independent lines and predict improved neural function in vivo?
Notes: Original experimental paper and GEO citation explicitly match OSD-999 and OSD-1000 study titles.

Title: Proteomic dataset of MECP2-deficient and wild-type human brain organoids under spaceflight and ground conditions
One sentence finding: A dataset descriptor released roughly 5,952 protein groups from spaceflown and ground human brain organoids with and without MECP2 deficiency.
One sentence remaining question: Which genotype-by-flight protein changes are robust, and do they have independent functional confirmation?
Notes: Data descriptor, not a study proving a functional mechanism; paper reports nine LC-MS/MS acquisitions from two individual lines.

Title: A ferroptosis-related transcriptional signature in the brain after a 35-day spaceflight
One sentence finding: Reanalysis of four regional datasets identified hippocampal, particularly dentate-gyrus, ferroptosis-related expression signatures after spaceflight.
One sentence remaining question: Are these RNA signatures accompanied by iron-dependent lipid peroxidation and actual ferroptotic cell death?
Notes: Source paper explicitly identifies all four accession IDs; transcriptomic pathway inference is not evidence of cell death.

Title: Artificial Gravity Attenuates the Transcriptomic Response to Spaceflight in the Optic Nerve and Retina
One sentence finding: On-orbit artificial gravity attenuated transcriptomic alterations in mouse optic nerve and retina in a gravity-level-dependent pattern.
One sentence remaining question: Does graded artificial gravity preserve neurological or visual function rather than only RNA expression?
Notes: Original report cites 5–6 animals per flight gravity level and 12 habitat controls; optic nerve and retina are not equivalent to brain.

Title: Non-DNA radiosensitive targets that initiate persistent behavioral deficits in rats exposed to space radiation
One sentence finding: Radiation-induced behavioural deficits in rats tracked particle fluence in patterns suggestive of sensitive targets smaller than cell nuclei.
One sentence remaining question: Which membranes or other subcellular structures causally mediate these dose- and particle-dependent behavioural changes?
Notes: NASA archive explicitly lists four OSD accessions; targeted molecular data cannot be assumed from behavioural datasets.

Title: Prediction of Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) Pressure with Generative Adversarial Network Synthetic Plasma-CSF Biomarker Pairing
One sentence finding: A machine-learning study explored prediction of CSF pressure using plasma–CSF biomarker information and synthetic pairing.
One sentence remaining question: Does its model predict independently measured CSF pressure in an external human cohort or astronauts?
Notes: NASA archive lists both accessions; no independent external pressure-labelled cohort was verified.

Title: Combined space stressors induce independent behavioral deficits predicted by early peripheral blood monocytes
One sentence finding: Simulated galactic cosmic radiation and housing conditions independently or interactively affected mouse cognition, while early blood monocytes improved some models of later deficits.
One sentence remaining question: Can blood monocytes predict cognitive deficits prospectively before behavioural impairment becomes detectable across sexes and space-stressor combinations?
Evidence status: Peer-reviewed article + matched NASA study-family title
Notes: NASA OSD-618 and OSD-640 are the behavioural and flow-cytometry components of the study with this exact title; publication DOI verified via PubMed and journal.

Title: The ex vivo human translaminar autonomous system to study spaceflight associated neuro-ocular syndrome pathogenesis
One sentence finding: An ex vivo human donor-eye system modelling intracranial and intraocular pressure gradients produced optic-nerve and retinal morphological, inflammatory and functional abnormalities.
One sentence remaining question: How accurately does this ex vivo pressure model predict SANS in astronauts across variable donor backgrounds and realistic time-varying pressure exposures?
Evidence status: NASA OSD-817 explicitly lists DOI; related study family
Notes: OSD-817 directly lists Peng et al.; OSD-815/816/818 share the translaminar-model investigation, but individual accession-to-paper metadata were not exhaustively rechecked.

Title: Polydopamine-Based Antioxidant Countermeasures Against Spaceflight-Induced Neurodegeneration
Type: Original study — related earlier mission, outside mapped OSDR accession inventory
One sentence finding: Polydopamine nanoparticles mitigated spaceflight-associated neuronal oxidative-stress and transcriptional alterations in a separate ISS neuron-like-cell experiment.
One sentence remaining question: Can antioxidant protection be reproduced with alternative chemistries and verified through neural functional outcomes beyond gene-expression rescue?
Evidence status: Peer-reviewed article; OSDR accession not mapped
Notes: The paper reports GEO GSE290701 for the original PROMETEO experiment; distinct from PROMETEO 2 (GSE295652 and OSD-1005). Do not assign OSD-1005 to this study.
